# CoLa2+EarthRanger

This tutorial generates a species distribution model (SDM) using CoLa new modules. You will use EarthRanger API (via ecoscope Python package)


```{r earthranger, opts.label=}
library(cola)

(wd <- file.path(Sys.getenv('COLA_DATA_PATH'), sessionIDgen(folder = TRUE)))
dir.create(wd)

erPoints <- file.path(wd, 'points.shp')
erRaster <- file.path(wd, 'raster.tif')
  
ERpoints <- earthRanger_py(
    server = 'https://twiga.pamdas.org', 
    username = 'IGonzalez', 
    pwd = 'temp12345',
    datefrom = '2026-09-06',
    dateto = '2026-12-16',
    subject = 'NAM_test',
    outshp = erPoints, 
    outtif = erRaster,
    dokde = 1,
    spatresinmeters = 10000)

```


```{r earthrangerplot}
library(terra)
rastLayer <- rast( erRaster )
plot(rastLayer, main = 'KDE')

vectLayer <- vect( erPoints )
dim(vectLayer)
plot(vectLayer, add = TRUE)
```

## Earth ranger

This is an R Markdown format used for publishing markdown documents to GitHub. When you click the **Knit** button all R code chunks are run and a markdown file (.md) suitable for publishing to GitHub is generated.

```{r upload}
cola2Upl <- localPoints2ee_py(
    ee_project = 'gonzalezivan',
    point_path = erRaster,
    ee_layer = 'projects/gonzalezivan/assets/cola2/erpoints',
    presence_col = NULL,
    num_abs = nrow(vectLayer))

```


## Including Code

You can include R code in the document as follows:

```{r extract}
cola::sdm_extract_py(, …)
```

```{r extract}
cola::sdm_extract_py(, …)
```

```{r extract}
cola::sdm_extract_py(predictor_source, …)
```

```{r fitting}
cola::sdm_model_fitting_py(predictor_source, …)
```

```{r prediction}
cola::sdm_prediction_py(predictor_source, …)
```

```{r download}
cola::export_ee2gd_py(username, …)
```




## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
